name: Gulf Shores Museum
description: The Gulf Shores Museum offers free admission to the public and features a variety of exhibits exploring the history and culture of Gulf Shores. The museum showcases permanent exhibits including 'Portrait of a Fishing Village' created by residents of the Lagoon Village detailing families who settled along the north side of Little Lagoon during the 19th Century, 'Drawing a Line in the Sand' commemorating the 50th Anniversary Celebration for the City of Gulf Shores in 2007, and 'Hurricanes - What you Need to Know' where guests can learn about hurricanes, their origins, the devastation they create, and how a community rebuilds following a hurricane. The museum also features rotating exhibits and special exhibits that can range from human interest stories to exhibits on loan from various institutions. Programs and events occur throughout the year and vary depending on holiday, event, or demand from the audience.
